name: Karakachan Horse
notes: The horse of the Karakachans, the transhumant pastoralists of the Balkans, and an indigenous Bulgarian mountain breed of the Rhodopes, Rila, Pirin, Stara Planina and Kraishte. It lives semi-free in herds year round and is one of the smallest horses in the mod.

Almost always bay or brown. This is the most visually unified natural pool that ships: chestnut and black are each held at a fraction of a percent, present only as an admission that no one has shown either locus to be fixed.
Every dilution, every white pattern, grey and the leopard complex are forced wild. A primitive mountain landrace is not a licence to seed primitive-looking alleles that nobody has tested for.

Size follows the measured exterior study - a mean of 130.22 cm, inside a modern range of roughly 126-138 cm - rather than the older descriptions nearer 128 cm. The population is reported as taller and heavier than it was a century ago.
Cold tolerant near-fixed: it winters out in the mountains, which is the whole of its reputation, and health 10 is that plus foaling and thriving on thin grazing with no shelter.
Listed as critically endangered on Bulgaria's Red Data List of autochthonous domestic forms. By 2018 the four Rhodope rewilding herds together held more than eighty horses.
All disorders clear. No Karakachan carrier data was located, and hardiness is not evidence of immunity any more than rarity is evidence of disease.
The hoof quality, the herd behaviour, the pack and transhumance work, and the rewilding programme itself are none of them modelled.
